subject: Diferences between beta in dummy regression and Delta Chisquare for means.

messages.author: 56a8aa4a45a311ff
messages.subject: Diferences between beta in dummy regression and Delta Chisquare for means.
parts:
Dear all,
I am puzzled with the following. I am comparing latent means for two groups. 
For the Delta Chi-square approach I am using this modeling:

MODEL 1

bd <-  readRDS("D:/OneDrive - NOVASBE/AMOS/exercicios/otocs.rds")

model <- 'OTOCS =~ OTOCS1 + OTOCS2 + OTOCS3 + OTOCS5
          OTOCS1 ~~ OTOCS2'
fitModML <-  sem(modelo, data=bd, group="País", ordered=T, group.equal=c("thresholds", "loadings", "intercepts"))
summary(fitModML, standardized=T, fit.measures=T)

So I get for group 2 an intercept estimate that is the difference between group 1 ( intercept =0) and group 2., that is -0.153. 

The other way to do it is to fit the MIMIC like model:

MODEL 2

modelM <- 'OTOCS =~ OTOCS1 + OTOCS2 + OTOCS3 + OTOCS5
          OTOCS1 ~~ OTOCS2
OTOCS ~ País '
fitMM <- sem(modelM, data=bd, ordered = T, std.lv=T)
summary(fitMM, standardized=T, rsquare=T)

But for this one I get a Beta=-0.17.

I know the differences are not that big. But I am wondering why the values are not the same? Probably because of the constraints imposed on the thresholds, loadings and intercepts in model 1?
I am attaching the df if you want to run the analysis...

Thanks for any insights.

João

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Diferences between beta in dummy regression and Delta Chisquare for means.
parts:
I haven't looked at your data, but in general the difference is likely due to different parameters being constrained to be equal between groups. In a MIMIC model like yours all parameters except the latent means are constrained to be equal across groups, but in a multiple group model you control which parameters are equal across groups and which are no equal, which gives you added flexibility in modeling your results. If you set every parameter but the latent mean to be equal across groups you should see the same mean difference. 

Alex

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Diferences between beta in dummy regression and Delta Chisquare for means.
parts:
Alex is right, MIMIC models assume homogeneity of residual and factor variances, whereas your multigroup model does not impose those constraints.
